lesson.text: Quick memory: a farm 5 m by 3 m has an area of 5 × 3 = 15 square metres. Area is the inside. Today: the fence round the outside!
Perimeter is the distance all the way round a shape. Walk round this farm: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 m of fence.
Add every side of any shape. This triangle: 5 + 4 + 5 = 14 cm.
A shape of squares: count the edges all the way round the outside. This L-shape has a perimeter of 16 units. Do not count the lines inside!
A missing side: the perimeter is 20 cm, and three sides are 6 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm. They make 16, so the missing side is 20 − 16 = 4 cm.
The same fence, different farms! A 2 by 6 farm and a 4 by 4 farm both have a fence of 16. But their areas are different: 12 and 16.
Build it: a farm with an area of 6 and a fence of 10 is 2 by 3. Next, in grade 4: area and perimeter of bigger farms.

exercises.prompt: What is the perimeter of the rectangle, in metres?
What is the perimeter of the triangle, in centimetres?
Each square is 1 cm long. What is the perimeter of the shape, in centimetres?
exercises.hint: Count the edges all the way round the outside.

exercises.prompt: The perimeter is measured all the way round the outside of a shape.
exercises.hint: Think of a fence round a farm.
exercises.explain: Yes: the perimeter is the distance all the way round.

exercises.prompt: What is the perimeter of a square with sides of 5 cm?
A square farm has sides of 3 m. How much fence goes all the way round, in metres?
What is the perimeter of the shape, in centimetres?
exercises.hint: Add every side, all the way round.

exercises.prompt: Each square is 1 cm long. What is the perimeter of the shape, in centimetres?
exercises.hint: Go round the outside and count every edge. Do not count the inside lines.
exercises.explain: All the way round the outside is 14 cm.

exercises.prompt: The perimeter of the shape is 24 cm. How long is the side marked ?, in centimetres?
exercises.hint: Add the sides you know, then take that away from 24.

exercises.prompt: Which rectangle has the same perimeter as a 3 m by 5 m rectangle?
exercises.hint: Add the two sides and double.
exercises.explain: 3 + 5 = 8 and 2 + 6 = 8, so both have a perimeter of 16 m.

exercises.prompt: Build a rectangle farm with an area of 6 squares and a fence of 10 all the way round.
exercises.hint: Which rectangles have an area of 6? Work out the fence of each one.
exercises.explain: 2 by 3: the area is 6 and the fence is 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 10.

exercises.prompt: A 1 by 9 farm and a 5 by 5 farm have the same perimeter.
The perimeter of the L-shape is 30 m. How long is the side marked ?, in metres?
exercises.hint: Add the sides you know, then take that away from 30.

exercises.prompt: What is the perimeter of the hexagon, in centimetres?
exercises.hint: All 6 sides are the same length.

exercises.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 26 m. One side is 8 m. How long is the side next to it, in metres?
exercises.hint: Two sides of 8 m make 16. Share what is left between the other two sides.

exercises.prompt: Build a rectangle farm with an area of 12 squares and a fence of 14 all the way round.
exercises.hint: Try each rectangle with an area of 12: 1 by 12, 2 by 6, 3 by 4. Which fence is 14?
exercises.explain: 3 by 4: the area is 12 and the fence is 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 = 14.

exercises.prompt: Three farms each have a fence of 12. Which one has the biggest area?
Two shapes with the same perimeter always have the same area.
exercises.hint: Think of a 1 by 5 farm and a 3 by 3 farm.
exercises.explain: Both have a fence of 12, but their areas are 5 and 9.
